mechanism: Combines supersampled rounded-rectangle body and rounded-triangle pointer on CCanvas with BUBBLE_ORIENTATION (up/down/left/right), scanline fills, segmented borders, and borderExtensionMultiplier joins. Chart UI chrome for alerts/tooltips only.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: n/a (bitmap label canvases; no market series)

quote: In Part 18, we combine these shapes to create rounded speech bubbles/balloons with orientation control, allowing pointers to face up, down, left, or right.

series_key: mql5 wizard techniques you should know
mechanism: Build 5×5 matrix of price changes for Mon–Fri × {Open, Weighted, Median, Close, Typical}; z-normalize; Cov(); Eig(); project P=M·Vᵀ; take row/col maxima of P to name the weekday and applied-price series that capture most variance (and minima for least). Use those as trade-day / MA-price filters so entries fire only on the variance-dominant day.
data_needed: OHLC(+typical/weighted/median) history into a square day×price-type matrix; z-norm, covariance, eigen decomposition; analysis window (article uses 2022 then validates 2023).
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURJPY D1 script example; EURUSD H4 script+EA (best=FRIDAY/PRICE_WEIGHTED, worst=TUESDAY/PRICE_OPEN); 2022–2024 tests
why_new_for_mis: Turns PCA into an explicit calendar×price-series regime sensor that ranks which weekday and quote type carry the symbol’s dominant variance—usable as an MIS gate without inventing a new indicator family.
quote: So, from our logs above we can see that Thursdays and Closing-price series are responsible for most of the variance in the price action of the symbol on whose chart the script is attached (the script was attached to EURJPY).

series_key: mql5 wizard techniques you should know
mechanism: Treat columns of a square returns matrix as candidate portfolios (e.g. SPY/TLT/PDBC allocation regimes); after z-norm→cov→eig, transpose-multiply to a projection matrix; pick the portfolio row whose max loading sits on the largest eigen value to perpetuate the dominant co-movement pattern (or the row loading on the smallest eigen to lean against it).
data_needed: Square multi-asset returns matrix (article: 5y ETF returns under 3 allocation vectors); z-norm, Cov, Eig, projection.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: SPY, TLT, PDBC illustrative 5-year returns; general n×n square matrices
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS a covariance-eigen portfolio sensor that ranks which allocation most continues (or opposes) the observed cross-asset variance structure.
quote: So, PCA with eigen vectors can filter out a portfolio from these that is most likely to continue this trend, as is the case with portfolio 1 or one to even do the reverse which in our case would be portfolio 3 since in the projection matrix the 3rd row’s maximum value is in column 3 and the 3rd eigen vector had the least value.

series_key: mql5 wizard techniques you should know
mechanism: Normalize raw eigen values to [0,1] (e.g. 2.94,1.92,0.14 → 0.588,0.384,0.028) and keep every eigen vector whose weight exceeds a threshold (e.g. 0.3), logging the paired matrix axes (weekday×price or layers×size) as a multi-setting list rather than only the single max.
data_needed: Eigen values from any PCA run; threshold hyperparameter; struct/array of matched (x,y) properties.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Same EURUSD H4 / matrix setups as companion PCA ideas; method is matrix-size agnostic
why_new_for_mis: Extends single-winner PCA into a multi-component variance sensor so MIS can track several co-dominant dimensions when more than one eigen exceeds a floor.
quote: Once this is done you can then define selection thresholds for the eigen vectors you will pick from each analysis. For example, if a PCA analysis of a 3 x 3 matrix initially gives the values 2.94, 1.92, 0.14 then we would normalize these values to a 0 – 1 range as: 0.588, 0.384, & 0.028.

mechanism: When PositionsTotal()==0, for each folio symbol copy two adjacent 30-bar close vectors and compute CorrCoef; keep the symbol with largest positive autocorrelation whose close[0] vs close[29] agrees with the RSI Direction sign; that symbol’s trend direction sets the first BUY/SELL.
data_needed: Multi-symbol close buffers (lag-0 and lag-30 windows of length 30); CorrCoef; primary signal Direction; folio symbol list with prefix/suffix.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Commodity folio AUDNZD,AUDUSD,AUDCAD,AUDJPY,NZDUSD,NZDCAD,NZDJPY,USDCAD,CADJPY; H4; tested on AUDJPY 2023–2024; RSI signal shared
why_new_for_mis: Provides a cross-sectional autocorrelation regime sensor that picks the strongest trending pair from a basket before committing capital.
quote: We use the largest positive value and not simply the magnitude because we are targeting trending symbols or the symbol with the strongest trend from the portfolio.

series_key: mql5 wizard techniques you should know
mechanism: With one open position in float<0, scan remaining folio symbols for max fabs(CorrCoef) of 30-bar closes vs the open symbol; open a second position on that highest-magnitude correlate in its own local trend direction—cross-market sequential hedge rather than parallel independent risk.
data_needed: Open-position profit and symbol; 30-bar close vectors for open and candidate symbols; absolute CorrCoef ranking.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Same 9-pair commodity folio; H4; 2023–2024 tests; fixed-lot money management
why_new_for_mis: Frames |correlation| to the open book as a live cross-market opportunity sensor MIS can use when a position is underwater.
quote: If the initial opened position is in drawdown, then we sift through the remaining portfolio symbols and try to find one with an effective ‘inverse’ correlation. ‘Inverse’ in the sense that we are only interested in magnitude, and we’ll follow the trend of this symbol as long as its correlation magnitude to the current open symbol is highest

mechanism: Populate a square matrix of mean |forward-pass error| for MLPs over hidden-layer count × hidden size (article: 1–10 layers × sizes 2–11) with default weights/biases and no backprop; z-norm→cov→eig; project; choose layer-count and size at the minima of the projection extrema (errors, not returns) as the NAS pick; control against maxima.
data_needed: Grid of Cnetwork instances; per-bar Norm(close changes) inputs/targets; accumulated fabs(output−target); ZNorm/Cov/Eig/projection.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURJPY H4, year 2022 screening (~2184 bars); input layer size 4 last closes → 1 next close; soft-plus activation; recommended 6×size-2 vs worst 9×size-4
why_new_for_mis: Replaces exhaustive train-and-score NAS with an eigen scan over forward-error coordinates—cheap architecture sensing for sequence price models MIS might deploy.
quote: Since for testing purposes we want to use the network with the least error, our selections for network by number of layers and size of each layer will be the minimums in each of the eigen vectors as retrieved from the projection matrix.

series_key: mql5 wizard techniques you should know
mechanism: Norm(A,B) maps paired price vectors into (0,1) with 0.5 = flat change, >0.5 rise, <0.5 drop via ±0.5·|Δ|/max(A,B)—so a small MLP can train next-close direction/magnitude without needing large bipolar output capacity.
data_needed: Paired new/old close (or feature) vectors of equal positive length; per-element signed fractional change.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURJPY H4 closes in the NAS script/EA; generalizable to any positive price series
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS a compact signed-change encoding that keeps neural price sensors in a bounded half-up/half-down range suitable for modest architectures.
quote: a 0.5 reading implies the resulting price change was 0 while any value less than 0.5 would indicate a resulting price drop and a value above 0.5 would point to a rise in price.

mechanism: For each day, size vectors m_asia/m_europe/m_america to (High−Low)/point; for every intraday bar, map low→high into point boxes and increment the session vector by hour (≥AmericaStart → America; EuropeStart..America → Europe; else Asia). Stacked histograms total=asia+europe+america and europe_asia=asia+europe encode time-at-price by session.
data_needed: Daily High/Low; intraday MqlRates for the day; SYMBOL_POINT; session start hours (default Europe 8, America 14).
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Chart Symbol(); PERIOD_D1 day bounds with PERIOD_CURRENT intraday bars; default InpShowDays=7; M30 example with 3 days in intro
why_new_for_mis: Operationalizes Market Profile as session-conditioned liquidity/time-at-price vectors MIS can read as sensors, not just chart decoration—even though this part focuses on canvas delivery.
quote: The point here is to count and write into the array (vector) cells the number of bars that cross each price level calculated in points from Low to High of the day.
